title: Who Let Him Back
narrativeQuestion: When a famous athlete serves his sentence, which second chances does he deserve: a job, an honor, both or neither?

chapters.title: Run it back
chapters.claim: Recap of 23 Months through eight dated cards from the 2001 draft to the 2024 Norfolk State hire.

chapters.title: What happened to the dogs
chapters.claim: Of 51 pit bulls held in the federal case, 47 were placed after individual evaluation, 22 of them at Best Friends in Utah. In April 2009 national groups changed their policy on dogs seized from fighting rings.

chapters.title: The rules changed around him
chapters.claim: Federal dogfighting law was strengthened in 2007, 2008 and 2014, and Vick lobbied Congress in 2011.

chapters.title: Two apologies
chapters.claim: Vick's 2007 statement did not apologize to the dogs. In 2009 on 60 Minutes he said he should have stopped it and deserved to lose the $130 million.

chapters.title: The swoosh comes back
chapters.claim: Nike ended Vick's deal in August 2007 and signed him again on July 1, 2011.

chapters.title: You make the call
chapters.claim: Seven real decisions from 2009 to 2026 split into jobs and honors.

accuracyNotes: Dog counts follow Best Friends Animal Society: 51 pit bulls in the case, 47 placed, 22 to Best Friends, the rest to seven other groups.
Norfolk State record stated as of mid October 2026.
